Rokiskis Jewish Сemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžys County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Rokiskis was one of the few places in Lithuania to serve as a center for Chabad Hasidism, maintaining separate rabbis for its Hasidic and Mitnagdim communities before WWI; in February 1931, the Lubavitcher Rebbe himself visited the town, drawing many visitors. Near the main street stood three distinctively colored synagogues — yellow for scholars, green for property owners, and red, the largest, for ordinary townspeople — matching the colors of the Lithuanian national flag. The town was the birthplace of Yakov Smushkevich, commander-in-chief of the Soviet Air Force in 1939–40, a hero of the Spanish Civil War known as 'General Douglas,' and the first Jew ever awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union, which he received twice. The German army's own Jäger Report documents that 3,207 Jews were murdered near Bajorai village on August 15–16, 1941. A new gate, fence, and memorial stone were installed at this cemetery in September 2013, engraved by sculptor Albertas Jasiūnas with a trilingual inscription from Ecclesiastes.
